summary: Iteration 64 — Backend-only tests for anti-block send-gate covering ALL automatic non-bot sends. 12/12 tests passed. Validated services.send_gate.acquire_send_slot / record_send semantics (disabled bypass, hourly/daily limits, cadence, burst pause, escalation, hour-boundary reset) and integration with scheduler._process_billing_reminders / _process_reminders / _process_surveys (each correctly aborts remaining sends when the gate returns False). Regression on GET/PUT /api/crm/campaign-settings passed.
critical_code_review_comments: scheduler._process_reminders uses `break` on gate-blocked to stop iterating the cursor — correct behavior (avoids retrying same limit for every appointment) but could starve later companies within same tick if a single company has many pending appointments; iteration across companies still proceeds because the break is inside the async-for on appointments, not on companies. Verified OK.

services.send_gate._DEFAULTS.enabled=True whereas routes/crm_routes.py GET default also enabled=True — consistent. However campaign_settings default hourly_limit differs between the two (send_gate defaults hourly_limit=50, GET default also 50). Good.

The burst_pause branch only triggers when day_count % burst_size == 0 AND day_count>0 — meaning after exactly burst_size messages, the (burst_size+1)th send is blocked until burst_pause_seconds elapse. Correct, but note escalation factor is applied to interval_min but NOT to burst_pause; consider documenting.
